To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the European Commission is currently working to standardize the interface between smart meters and consumers, that the most common communication protocols are based on the IEEE 802.15.4 standard, and that the most promising architectures for a proper interface between consumers and smart meters are based on a local area network (LAN) with the smart meter as gateway to the Internet of Things.

the smart meter network should be designed to be open and interoperable, with the possibility to add new devices, to integrate different technologies and to provide a proper interface to the household.

the European Union and international standards for the interface between smart meters and the final user have not been defined yet, but they are expected soon, that the most common interface solutions on the market are based on the Internet, that a proper consumer-oriented interface should be designed to allow for the implementation of the most common services, and that the implementation of a smart-metering network should be based on an efficient architecture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of an efficient and effective interface between smart meters and the households.

the following aspects: (i) the analysis of the existing smart metering architectures; (ii) the definition of the main requirements for a consumer-oriented implementation of smart metering systems; (iii) the proposal of an architecture that can be easily implemented and that can be adapted to different contexts and scenarios.

the definition of a smart meter interface that can provide a proper and efficient interface between the household and the smart meter system, by considering the actual needs and the technological capabilities of the final user, in order to improve the acceptance and the usability of the smart meter system and, consequently, its actual impact in terms of energy savings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the smart meter interface is a complex issue that requires a multidisciplinary and multi-stakeholder approach, and that the definition of a proper interface is still an open issue.

, while the smart meters and their interconnection are already available on the market and can be implemented in the next future, a proper consumer-oriented interface should be implemented, and, in the meanwhile, a proper communication infrastructure should be set up to allow a fast and efficient implementation of such interface.

a smart meter network should be designed in order to offer the final user an interface which is easy and natural to use, and that it should be based on a set of services which can be easily understood, and which are relevant for the user.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the smart meter network is not only a technical network, it also needs to be a social network, in order to be able to provide a proper interface to the final users.
the smart meters should be considered as a part of the home automation system, and not as stand-alone devices.
the smart meter network should be designed to be open, flexible, secure, and easy to use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local interface is a critical element for the success of a large-scale smart meter deployment.
a smart meter network can be implemented by following a simple and well-defined set of rules.
the local interface should be implemented as a local area network (LAN) with an open protocol and a proper security level.
